sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. randomized experiment with fixed finite stratum set \(\mathcal J\), fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A\), and known action probabilities \(e_{ja}\).
sampling_model.units: For each local row \(n\), the full units \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_n\), while the planner observes only \(O^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ni}=(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni})\) and hence only \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditional randomization satisfies \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), consistency, and \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every stratum has \(p_j\ge p_{\min}\), every randomized action has \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\), and every benchmark action has \(b_{ja}\ge\beta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite randomized cells are estimated by within-cell Hájek means and stratum masses by empirical frequencies. These observed estimators generate \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), the only frontier supplied to the temperature selector. The Gaussian approximation envelope for the distinct oracle regret path is derived from bounded outcomes, cell mass, and overlap in \(\mathrm{lem:cell\mbox{-}gaussian}\), rather than assumed for the estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: No uniform atom-removed modulus, and hence no modulus-based uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion, is available over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class because it contains the fixed binary collision witness.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

body.tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. On the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass, the main positive result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this nonlinear path, and an observed plug-in welfare frontier supplies an operational temperature selector. A finite interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm emits a machine-checkable one-sided certificate with an analytic fallback, so the simultaneous envelope remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. These positive results are not claimed over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. Conversely, a legal fixed binary collision witness lies in that broader class, so the failure of uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, and of every modulus-based uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion, transfers upward.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while hard assignment boundaries and softmax inference for predetermined smoothing sequences are studied separately. No published result supplies a quantitative joint path law or a certified one-sided critical value over the full penalty menu on the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass. Standard Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration also does not cover the hard-cell atom collisions exhibited here; because the binary witness satisfies the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie hypotheses, enlarging to that class cannot recover a uniform atom-removed modulus.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, the hard endpoint is directionally irregular with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and the opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization. The fixed finite-cell structure supports the positive approximation and certified computation. The same structure contains a binary atom-collision witness, which is enough for an upward negative transfer even though positive achievability does not transfer upward.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a verified lower CDF bracket with directed rounding and a finite fallback into computably honest inference after temperature choice. It also proves the hard-cell atom formula, constructs a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, and proves the asymmetric class-transfer corollary: positive results remain on the finite-cell subclass, whereas the impossibility and every modulus-based critical-value obstruction extend to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.

body.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. The positive path law and certified calibration here are restricted to the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass and are not asserted over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The relation reverses for the negative result: the fixed two-stratum binary collision design satisfies their randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so a uniform atom-removed modulus or any modulus-based probability-to-critical-value conversion over their broader class would contradict the witness theorem. Their three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, not a finite-stratification adequacy claim. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing for one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature, a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing give anti-concentration for Gaussian-process suprema, whereas \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear and has the proved hard-cell atom collisions. Fang--Santos explains directional irregularity but does not furnish atom-safe continuum calibration. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian integration components, not certification of this nonlinear continuum event. Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic for an observed series path; the present bridge additionally separates the observed selector frontier from the unobserved oracle causal-regret target.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage on its declared finite-cell inputs because work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback. It need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). The fixed two-stratum binary witness shows that no uniform atom-removed modulus follows even over the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class: distinct positive hard-cell atoms can collide while retaining positive mass. Thus a modulus-based two-sided value-width certificate would need additional atom separation, a restricted local-state set, or another explicit structural condition. This is an upward transfer only for the obstruction; it does not broaden the positive approximation or calibration theorem. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
body.honest_scope: The positive path-law and causal calibration results are uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and covariance spectra bounded away from zero. They exclude boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. They are not claimed over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; that frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The negative scope is broader: the fixed binary witness already satisfies the Fang--Ridder--Xie randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so the no-modulus result and every modulus-based probability-to-critical-value obstruction transfer upward. No non-modulus impossibility theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: The positive output is deliberately one-sided and subclass-specific: for the declared fixed finite-cell randomized model, it certifies that the entire normalized oracle-regret path lies below one auditable critical value, so any temperature selected measurably from observed data inherits the same guarantee. No such positive path law or causal calibration claim is made for the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The negative conclusion does extend: nearby local states in a fixed binary design belonging to that broader class place positive hard-cell atoms arbitrarily close together. Thus moving to the broader class cannot create a uniform atom-removed modulus or a modulus-based uniform conversion from probability error to critical-value error.
